billet_4.name: Concept magnet, pulsed
billet_4.blurb: The note's own magnet, swung to full field on every shot.
warnings: the winding quenches every pulse: the tape cannot carry the current at this field even before it is pulsed (no enthalpy margin)
no reinforcement keeps the REBCO within its strain limit at 3.66 GPa of hoop stress
notes: needs 100.3 T from a superconducting winding: the all-superconducting record is 35.6 T and no superconductor has carried current above 48.7 T
peak hoop stress 3.66 GPa needs a composite modulus of 1373 GPa at the 0.4 % strain limit
field must rise in 10.3 ms for this workpiece: 9.77e+03 T/s

billet_4.name: Concept magnet, steady
billet_4.blurb: The same magnet held at constant field.
warnings: a steady field exerts no pressure on a stationary, non-magnetic workpiece
notes: a steady field has diffused into the workpiece: (B_out^2 - B_in^2)/(2 mu0) = 0, so the magnet exerts no forming pressure however strong it is
as a magnet alone it would still be infeasible (conductor and structure)

billet_4.name: Resistive pulsed magnet
billet_4.blurb: A reinforced copper-alloy coil fired from a capacitor bank: the technology of the 100 T record.
notes: 100.3 T in a 100 mm bore: extrapolation (the 100.75 T record is in a 10 mm bore; stored energy grows with bore volume)
at the 10.3 ms rise the workpiece needs: 38 turn(s), 24.94 kV, 1.23 MA, 15.46 GW, 102 MJ bank (extrapolation)
the supply could go as fast as 2.15 ms within demonstrated practice: it keeps up with this workpiece

billet_4.name: Hybrid: steady background plus pulsed insert
billet_4.blurb: A steady superconducting outsert with a pulsed copper insert inside it.
warnings: the insert's pulsed flux is 2.66x the background's own: a shorted background would be driven through zero and reversed (30.5 T swing at 2.98e+03 T/s) unless the insert is flux-compensated
notes: 11.5 T steady background plus a 89.42 T pulse: total 100.9 T at the insert (more than the 100.3 T of an unbiased pulse) for the same pressure
the bias cuts the insert's own field energy by 20%; the peak field and stress on the insert are not relieved
background magnet: 11.5 T in a 550 mm bore (state of the art)
open-circuit, the pulse induces 707 V on every background turn

billet_4.name: Single-turn destructive coil
billet_4.blurb: A copper strip and a very fast bank. Reaches these fields for microseconds and is destroyed doing it.
warnings: the coil is consumed by every shot
notes: one turn, 100 mm long: 7.979 MA in 2.5 us, 494.8 kV, 3.14 MJ in the bore field
the coil is destroyed by every shot (it explodes outward); samples in existing 20 mm systems usually survive
the field lasts microseconds: the load on the workpiece is a shock, not a press stroke

billet_4.name: Industrial forming coil
billet_4.blurb: Today's forming coil, run at its field limit over the same bore.
warnings: capped at 50 T: delivers 0.995 GPa of the 4 GPa asked for
not an industrial machine at this size: peak current extrapolation, coil heating extrapolation
notes: industrial electromagnetic forming works at 20-50 T on areas of square centimetres with 10-100 kJ machines (Psyk et al. 2011)
over this bore and length at a 50 us rise: 5.07 MJ, 15.52 kV, 20.46 MA (extrapolation)
